overall_summary: Heavy geopolitical risks from US-Iran strikes, Hormuz disruption, and oil supply threats are driving a risk-off tone that overshadows crypto. Bitcoin showed resilience with ETF inflows and a break above 65k, yet rising yields and growth warnings keep the broader setup fragile. Traders face clear macro headwinds despite selective crypto positives.
key_points: US-Iran conflict and Hormuz risks escalate sharply
Oil surges and World Bank cuts growth outlook
Bitcoin ETFs log sixth inflow day, clears 65k
Corporate Bitcoin setbacks as holdings face liquidation

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Log Sixth Straight Inflow Day, $203M Added
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in two hundred three million dollars on Tuesday, extending the inflow streak to six sessions and roughly nine hundred thirty million dollars total. That is the longest consecutive run since April. Bitcoin traded above sixty-five thousand and briefly tagged sixty-six seven hundred as Fear and Greed moved out of extreme fear. Traders should care because sustained institutional buying after a brutal summer of outflows is the clearest demand signal we have right now and supports holding the sixty-five k zone.
items.impact: Supports BTC above 65k and could fuel further upside if streak continues

items.title: Jack Mallers Exits Twenty One Capital; Tether Merger Collapses
items.summary: Jack Mallers stepped down as CEO of Tether-backed Twenty One Capital effective July twentieth, returning focus to Strike. The planned three-way merger combining Twenty One, Strike, and Elektron Energy has been abandoned. Raphael Zagury takes over as CEO. This matters because it undercuts the corporate Bitcoin treasury narrative that had been a secondary demand driver alongside ETFs, and stock reaction was negative.
items.impact: Weighs on Bitcoin treasury company valuations and related sentiment

items.title: Satsuma Shareholders Vote to Liquidate Bitcoin Holdings
items.summary: Satsuma Technology shareholders approved selling the company's six hundred sixty-eight Bitcoin and delisting from the London Stock Exchange. This comes less than a year after raising roughly two hundred eighteen million dollars for a Bitcoin treasury strategy. Shares had already collapsed more than ninety-nine percent from peak. Traders should watch because it is another visible unwind of a corporate BTC stack that can add spot supply and reinforce caution around treasury plays.
items.impact: Adds potential spot selling pressure and hurts treasury-company narrative

items.title: CLARITY Act Odds and Hougan Comment Lift Regulatory Hopes
items.summary: Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan said the market is now underestimating CLARITY Act passage odds and that if it clears, winter is over. Polymarket odds hover around forty to fifty-three percent for 2026 passage. Earlier chatter noted progress toward the Senate floor and White House movement on ethics language. This remains unresolved ahead of the August recess deadline, so it is a swing factor rather than a done deal, but positive headlines have already helped price action near sixty-five k.
items.impact: Potential major catalyst if floor vote materializes; currently sentiment support only

items.title: CoinShares Launches Europe Bitcoin Mining UCITS ETF
items.summary: CoinShares has debuted its first Bitcoin mining UCITS ETF, now trading on Deutsche Börse Xetra. It offers European institutions compliant equity exposure to the high-beta mining sector rather than spot Bitcoin. This expands the product toolkit for traditional allocators who want leveraged upside to a BTC rally through listed miners. Watch early flows as a tell for European institutional interest returning.
items.impact: Broadens institutional access and could boost miner equities on BTC strength

items.title: Bitcoin Clears 65k Resistance Amid Short Liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin broke and held above the sixty-five thousand level that had rejected price multiple times in July, briefly reaching toward sixty-six seven hundred. Reports cited hundreds of millions in liquidations, heavily weighted to shorts, as the move unfolded alongside the ETF inflow streak. Traders care because a confirmed hold above this zone strengthens the case for a sustained recovery attempt after the summer lows near fifty-eight k.
items.impact: Technical breakout confirmation could trigger further short covering and momentum

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Hits 2-Month High Near 4.64%
items.summary: Treasury yields climbed to two-month highs with the 10-year around 4.63 to 4.64 percent as escalating US-Iran hostilities pushed oil higher and revived inflation worries. President Trump downplayed near-term peace talks while supply risks mounted from the region and related disruptions. Traders should care because elevated yields tighten financial conditions, raise the discount rate on risk assets, and keep the dollar supported, all of which typically pressure Bitcoin and equities until the geopolitical premium eases.
items.impact: Higher yields and inflation fears weigh on risk assets and crypto

items.title: Oil Surges on Renewed US-Iran Tensions
items.summary: Brent crude jumped roughly 4 percent toward 95 dollars a barrel and WTI rose sharply as Middle East fighting intensified, Trump signaled Iran would pay for US deaths, and peace prospects dimmed. Higher energy prices feed directly into inflation readings and complicate the Fed path. Crypto traders need to watch this because sticky oil keeps rate-cut hopes distant and can trigger risk-off moves across markets.
items.impact: Elevated oil sustains inflation premium and tighter policy bets

items.title: UK CPI Cools to 2.6% in June
items.summary: UK consumer price inflation slowed to 2.6 percent year-over-year in June from 2.8 percent, coming in below the 2.7 percent consensus, helped by lower fuel prices. Core measures were mixed but the headline drop eases pressure on the Bank of England. This matters for global risk sentiment as softer UK inflation supports easier policy abroad and can lift sterling-sensitive assets while providing a modest tailwind for broader markets.
items.impact: Supports BoE easing hopes and mild risk-on tone

items.title: Fed Hold Expected Next Week; Sept Hike Odds Elevated
items.summary: Markets price a high probability the Fed holds the funds rate at 3.50 to 3.75 percent at the July 28-29 meeting, though odds of a hike later in the year remain material amid oil-driven inflation risks. Chair Warsh has emphasized price stability. Traders should track this closely because any shift in the higher-for-longer narrative directly affects liquidity conditions and Bitcoin's sensitivity to real rates.
items.impact: Near-term hold priced; path depends on oil and data

items.title: MBA Mortgage Apps Rise 1.9% Despite Higher Rates
items.summary: Mortgage applications rebounded 1.9 percent in the week ending July 17 even as the 30-year fixed rate climbed to 6.69 percent, a multi-month high. Purchase activity improved while refinances softened. This shows housing demand has some resilience, which supports the soft-landing view but also keeps the Fed cautious on cuts if activity stays firm.
items.impact: Housing data mixed; rates still restrictive

items.title: DXY Firm Near 101; 20-Year Auction and EIA Due Today
items.summary: The US dollar index held firm around 101 as yields stayed elevated. Today's calendar features the EIA crude inventories report, expected to show a draw, the 20-year Treasury bond auction, and remarks from President Trump. These events can swing yields, the dollar, and oil, creating volatility for crypto which often moves inversely to the greenback and real rates.
items.impact: Watch auction demand and inventory for yield/dollar moves

items.title: US Strikes Iran 11th Night as Hormuz Traffic Collapses
items.summary: The US military completed its eleventh consecutive night of strikes on Iranian targets including maritime capabilities and drone facilities, while Iran hit back at US sites in Gulf states. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz fell to just a handful of vessels with no major oil or LNG tankers crossing, driving Brent crude above 95 dollars a barrel. Traders should care because this is choking a fifth of global oil supply and fueling energy inflation that hits risk assets hard.
items.impact: Higher oil prices and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: Houthis Declare Red Sea Blockade on Saudi Oil
items.summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis vowed to blockade Saudi Arabian oil shipments through the Bab el-Mandeb strait and warned shipping firms against using Saudi ports. Two Saudi crude tankers bound for Asia immediately made U-turns. This opens a second major chokepoint alongside Hormuz and widens the US-Iran conflict, raising the odds of broader energy disruptions that squeeze global growth and markets.
items.impact: Further oil supply fears and shipping cost spikes

items.title: World Bank Warns War Could Cut Global Growth to 1.3%
items.summary: World Bank chief economist Indermit Gill said the escalating US-Iran conflict is already nearing the bank's worst-case scenario, which would slash 2026 global growth to 1.3 percent from recent forecasts near 2.5-3 percent while pushing inflation higher. Prolonged fighting risks higher rates, food insecurity, and debt distress for dozens of countries. Crypto traders watch this closely as it signals tighter financial conditions and weaker risk appetite ahead.
items.impact: Macro headwinds and potential rate hikes weighing on risk assets

items.title: Zelenskyy Fires Ukraine Army Chief Amid Protests
items.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy dismissed Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi and appointed Major General Mykhailo Drapatyi after days of protests sparked by earlier leadership changes and strategic disputes. The shake-up comes as Russia presses its offensive and highlights internal wartime tensions. For markets it adds uncertainty to the long-running Europe energy and security picture that already influences global risk sentiment.
items.impact: Limited direct crypto move but adds to geopolitical noise

items.title: Trump Imposes 50% Tariffs on Canada, Eyes More Duties
items.summary: The Trump administration announced new 50 percent tariffs on nearly 20 billion dollars of Canadian goods over alleged discrimination against US exports, effective next month, while US-Mexico talks on the USMCA continue. Fresh tariffs on dozens of other countries are expected soon as the temporary 10 percent global tariff expires Friday. Trade escalation raises inflation risks and hits supply chains, typically negative for risk assets including crypto.
items.impact: Trade war fears and higher costs pressuring markets

items.title: Rubio Says US Will Keep Hitting Iran Over Hormuz Control
items.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the United States will continue strikes as long as Iran tries to control the Strait of Hormuz and called Tehran not serious about diplomacy despite some outreach. Oil jumped over 4 percent on the comments with no ceasefire in sight. Prolonged conflict keeps energy prices elevated and supports a risk-off environment that crypto traders must factor into positioning.
items.impact: Sustained oil spike and geopolitical risk premium
